lactate-dehydrogenase.short: The enzyme that turns pyruvate and NADH into lactate and NAD⁺, and back. Very active and close to equilibrium, so some lactate forms whenever glycolysis runs.

lactate-shuttle.short: Brooks' idea that lactate made in one place is used in another: between cells (fast fibres to slow fibres, heart, brain, liver) and, more debated, inside a cell (cytosol to mitochondria).

mct.short: Membrane carriers that move lactate together with an H⁺. MCT1 (oxidative fibres, heart) mostly takes lactate up; MCT4 (fast fibres) mostly pushes it out.

gluconeogenesis.short: Making new glucose from non-carbohydrate building blocks, mainly in the liver (and kidneys). Lactate is its main raw material.

cori-cycle.short: Lactate from muscle travels in the blood to the liver, is turned back into glucose, and the glucose returns to the muscle.

metabolic-clearance-rate.short: The volume of blood cleared of lactate per minute (mL·kg⁻¹·min⁻¹). Removal rate = MCR × blood lactate concentration.

inorganic-phosphate.short: Free phosphate released when ATP and PCr are split. It builds up in hard exercise and is a leading cause of fatigue inside the muscle fibre.

rate-of-appearance.short: How fast lactate enters the blood (Ra) and leaves it (Rd). Blood lactate rises only when Ra exceeds Rd.

lactate-curve.short: Blood lactate plotted against power or speed in a step test: flat at first, then rising faster and faster. Its two bends are the lactate thresholds.
